tools.description: Search or filter the layout catalog to find a specific layout. Returns metadata only, no HTML. Each entry has position (opener/middle/closer: its role in a deck), when_to_use and when_not_to_use: read them to check the layout fits the content before choosing it. tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: Search or filter the theme catalog. Returns metadata and key colors only, not the full CSS. With an API key, the user's own saved themes (My Themes, id "custom:...") come last with custom: true; their ids work anywhere a theme id does.

tools.name: get_layout
tools.description: Return one layout as a ready-to-use, self-contained document: HTML, theme CSS, and its slot definitions. Call this once the user knows which layout they want, or with ids returned by suggest_deck.

tools.name: get_theme
tools.description: Return one theme in full: its complete CSS and design tokens.

tools.name: get_starter_kit
tools.description: Call this when joining several fetched layouts into one deck file. Requests like "merge these into one file", "bundle it as a deck", or "make it one HTML" mean this tool. Returns the base CSS, assembly rules, spacing tokens, and a viewport snippet for standalone viewing.

tools.name: suggest_deck
tools.description: Compose a deck and return a preview link the user can open in the browser right away. The user sees what the finished deck looks like without a single file being generated. tools.name: render_slide
tools.description: Fill one layout with your text and get back a finished, self-contained HTML document (theme, base and contract CSS inlined) that renders correctly when opened. Use it instead of get_layout when you already know the text: you do not assemble CSS or edit the markup yourself. Input: layout_id, optional

tools.name: check_slots
tools.description: Validate slot text against a layout before rendering. Nothing is rendered and no CSS is returned, so it is cheap: run it on every slide you wrote, fix what it reports, then call render_slide. Input: layout_id and slots (slot id to text), the same as render_slide. Returns { layout_id, ok, error_count

tools.description: Turn a deck into a downloadable .pptx file. Requests like "make it a PowerPoint", "PPT로 뽑아줘", or "export this deck" mean this tool. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "suggest_deck" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_layouts, get_layout, get_starter_kit, render_slide, check_slots, list_templates, get_template, list_pending_reviews, get_template_feedback · Private data: list_themes, get_layout, get_theme, get_starter_kit, suggest_deck, render_slide, export_pptx, list_templates, get_template, list_media, add_objects, list_pending_reviews, get_template_feedback · Public sink: list_media, update_objects, list_pending_reviews · Destructive: check_slots, remove_objects.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_layouts, get_layout, get_starter_kit, render_slide, check_slots, list_templates, get_template, list_pending_reviews, get_template_feedback · Private data: list_themes, get_layout, get_theme, get_starter_kit, suggest_deck, render_slide, export_pptx, list_templates, get_template, list_media, add_objects, list_pending_reviews, get_template_feedback · Public sink: list_media, update_objects, list_pending_reviews · Destructive: check_slots, remove_objects

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
